claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts.

In CodePipeline `SUPERSEDED` mode, a queued execution waiting behind a busy CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment rather than colliding with one in progress.
Setting the CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue so each runs in turn rather than being superseded by later executions.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (pipelineType V2).
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` on a pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The page links to the `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` registry API docs at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ and says the resource is described below on the page.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment, which can prevent concurrent runs of a deployment job that targets that environment.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is set at the stage level to control how the stage behaves with an exclusive lock check on the environment it references.
The Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` setting defaults to `runLatest`, and also accepts `sequential`.
With Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over rather than eventually applied.
With Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time in the same way as `sequential` lock behavior.
The `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource in the Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry can manage the exclusive lock check as code.
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and documents update conflicts.
The link target /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists in the Pulumi Registry.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command: up`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `args: --yes` passed to `pulumi up`.
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs target the same Pulumi stack, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
The page links to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ as the update conflict documentation.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' located under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0, meaning unlimited.

Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack update lease gives one-at-a-time behavior for updates to a stack.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes deployments (runs them one at a time).
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior: sequential` is a valid setting on a stage, used together with an environment exclusive lock check so that queued runs execute sequentially.

AWS CodePipeline pipelines have an execution mode setting that can be set to `QUEUED`, so waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older execution that is still waiting to start.
